clue.text: First-rate spinner following advice

indicators.note: the spinner comes after the advice, so it is placed second in the charade

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A slow bowler praised as excellent after some coaching tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal adjective for something of the highest quality, excellent.

clue.text: Heat's used to protect one's plants

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: heat means anger, and ires is a plural of ire
one is I, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: Warmth is employed to shield someone's garden flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowering plants with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Peg, over the summer, getting no supper!

indicators.note: in a down clue over means above, so the peg comes first

parts.note: a tee is a peg used to hold a golf ball
read as sum-mer, one who sums, a totaller

explanation.surface: A peg is driven in during the summer and no evening meal follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is misread as the season; it is one who does sums. 'no supper' means not one who sups, that is drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller never drinks alcohol, so never sups, playing on sup meaning drink.

clue.text: His groundbreaking work put pressure on mere mortal

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the pressure comes first

parts.note: a mere is a lake, and a lough is an Irish lake
a man is a mortal human being

explanation.surface: Applying pressure on ordinary people as part of pioneering work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaking' suggests innovation but is literal: breaking up soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploughman's work is ploughing, literally breaking the ground.

clue.text: Keen to raise bird for fighting

parts.note: game means willing or eager, as in game for anything
to cock is to tilt up or raise, as an eyebrow or a hat

explanation.surface: An enthusiast eager to breed birds for cockfights.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamecock is a cockerel bred and trained for cockfighting.

clue.text: Angry phone-in hosts being ordered to escort Alice

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the answer is inside these words

explanation.surface: An angry radio phone-in is told to accompany a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, the Queen orders this creature to take Alice to see the Mock Turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gryphon in Alice in Wonderland is commanded by the Queen of Hearts to lead Alice to the Mock Turtle.

clue.text: US authority opposed to blocking name change

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the way, so one piece sits inside the other
change suggests altering, so the letters of name are rearranged

parts.note: V is short for versus, meaning opposed to

explanation.surface: An American expert stands in the way of renaming something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns NAME into MAEN, and 'blocking' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A maven is an American term for an expert or connoisseur, an authority on a subject.

clue.text: Not exactly King's estate, perhaps

parts.note: CA is short for circa, meaning about or not exactly
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Whether this land really belongs to the monarch is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'estate' reads as a landed property but is an estate car, a station wagon, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a type of car with a large rear load space, known as a station wagon in the US.

clue.text: Blow brings warmth after brief lull

indicators.note: the warmth comes after the lull, so it is placed second
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a calm is a lull or quiet spell
amity means friendly warmth between people

explanation.surface: Bad weather brings warmer air after a short calm spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster or severe blow.

clue.text: Spiv smuggling diamonds in form of aircraft

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside, so the diamonds go within the spiv

parts.note: a wide boy is British slang for a flashy petty crook or spiv
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A shady dealer sneaks gems through customs on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv and a wide boy are both British terms for a flashy small-time crook dealing in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-body is a large jet airliner with two aisles, so a type of aircraft design.

clue.text: Having energy and velocity shown with one needle

parts.note: V is the standard symbol for velocity in physics
I is the Roman numeral for one
to needle someone is to annoy or rile them

explanation.surface: Something energetic and fast, paired with a single sharp point.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means vigorous and full of manly energy and strength.

clue.text: Take a while to fit in

definitions.meaning: to ... is to take a long time over something
to be accepted in a group or have a proper place

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to take a long time; as one word it means to fit in or be at home somewhere.

clue.text: Pleasing to see writing by true writer!

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: hand means handwriting, a person's style of writing
so means true, as in it is so
the writer of a clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Praising the good-looking script of an honest author.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'writer' is the setter, who in crosswords often refers to themself as ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes someone or something attractive and good-looking.

clue.text: Does its holder take his chance for a winning score?

definitions.text: Does its holder take his chance for a winning score?

parts.words: Does its holder take his chance for a winning score?
parts.note: score is read as to scratch, and its owner gambles on uncovering a winning combination on a lottery ticket

explanation.definitionFit: A scratchcard is a lottery ticket whose coating is scratched off to reveal whether it wins.

clue.text: Run at speed, overtaking several hundred cars

indicators.note: overtaking is read as taking over or going around, so the cars and hundreds sit within at

parts.note: taken as written
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, several hundred
Minis are small British cars
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Driving fast and passing hundreds of vehicles on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is a verb, meaning to manage, not a sprint. 'overtaking' places the hundreds and cars between the two letters of 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: To administrate is to manage or run an organisation or its affairs.

clue.text: Sort of pasta girl will enjoy?

parts.note: she refers to a girl
'll is the short form of will
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Will a girl enjoy this kind of pasta?
explanation.walkthrough: SHELL-LIKE is also British slang for the ear, as in a word in your shell-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta in the form of shells, like conchiglie, has a shell-like shape.

clue.text: Scottish churchgoers hear chilling confession

indicators.note: hear means the clue words are spoken, so their sound gives the letters

parts.note: we freeze is an admission that we are very cold

explanation.surface: Churchgoers in Scotland admit they are freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wee Frees are members of the Free Church of Scotland, a small conservative Presbyterian body.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee Frees is the nickname of members of the Free Church of Scotland.

clue.text: Two charges, including only son, with time to settle in

indicators.note: including means containing, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a fee is a charge, and two of them are needed
the second of the two fees
lone means only or single

explanation.surface: Two fees are levied, one covering an only child, with a deadline to get comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts LONE and S between the two FEEs, and T closes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel one's feet is an idiom for becoming confident and settled in a new situation.

clue.text: Bravely tinker with solicitor's input

indicators.note: input means put in, so the solicitor is placed within the tinker

parts.note: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a tout is someone who solicits for custom

explanation.surface: Courageously fixing something with a lawyer's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer but is one who solicits, a tout; 'tinker' is not the verb but Shakespeare's tinker Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoutly means bravely and resolutely, as in a stoutly defended position.

clue.text: A rod below runs deep

indicators.note: in a down clue below means placed underneath, so the rod comes last

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for runs in cricket
a cane is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A fishing rod hangs beneath fast-flowing deep water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs deep' reads as a phrase about water, but 'deep' alone defines, meaning profound or obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious and understood by few, so deep in the sense of profound.

clue.text: Order of tzar so emphatic, all of a sudden

indicators.note: order means arrangement, so the letters that follow are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler issues a forceful decree out of the blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzato is a musical direction meaning a note or chord is played with sudden, strong emphasis.

clue.text: Brother up for supporting card sharp

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath, so the card goes first

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A brother stands up for a card cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card sharp' reads as a cheat, but 'sharp' alone defines. 'up' turns BR into RB.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb means sour or harsh, sharp in taste or tone.

clue.text: Possible home for Pakistani prince returning to NW state

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the prince's name is read backwards

parts.note: Hal is Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
ORE is the abbreviation for Oregon, a state in the north-west USA

explanation.surface: A Pakistani prince heading home to the American north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, so somewhere a Pakistani might live.

clue.text: Judge English summer month dull

parts.note: June is a summer month in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: A judge finds an English summer month dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means dull, insipid and lacking interest or substance.

clue.text: Regularly used dustmen's truck

indicators.note: only every other letter is used, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Refuse collectors' usual vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: UTE is Australian short for utility vehicle, a pick-up truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A ute is a utility vehicle, a small pick-up truck in Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Clip associated with knitwear craft

parts.note: to trim is to clip or cut
Aran is a style of chunky cable-knit jumper from the Aran Islands of Ireland

explanation.surface: Snipping, as connected with a craft such as knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a boat with three hulls, a kind of sailing craft.

clue.text: Neglecting stomach, stubbornly blames poor diet

indicators.note: poor suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled
the stomach is the middle of the word, so leaving it out keeps only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone who won't own up to a bad eating plan blames everything except their belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neglecting stomach' keeps the outer S and Y of 'stubbornly'; 'poor' shuffles them with BLAMES. 'diet' looks like food but means a legislative assembly, as in Japan's Diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a formal legislative assembly or parliament, as in some countries.

clue.text: Sad news from press office circulated

indicators.note: the sad news comes from the press office, so the office's letters lead and the news follows

parts.note: ED stands for editor, the office in charge of a newspaper
news that someone died is sad news

explanation.surface: A press office announces a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddied means swirled round in circles, as water or air does in an eddy.
